topics.topic: Behavior when stale or partial backup temporary files cannot be removed
questions: If cleanup of a stale encrypted or decrypted temporary file fails, does the current run abort, continue its safe parts, or create new temporary files alongside it?

If a temporary or partial file cannot be removed, does the run abort, continue using different names, or continue despite the leftover file, and is the partial-file guarantee waived for cleanup failures?
Does failure to remove one stale temporary file abort startup, skip the current backup run, or allow the run to continue?

quotes:
A backup and its check file are
   written under temporary names in the backup location and become a kept
   backup only when complete; at every start and every run Registry first
   removes every temporary file left there, and a removal that fails is
   reported and tried again at the next run.

A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file, writes a
   diagnostic that names the failure and no value (A17), and is tried again at
   the next run; Registry keeps serving.
judgement.divergence: One implementation aborts or skips the current backup run after cleanup fails; another continues backup creation and retention deletion alongside the leftover file. The owner notices different backup availability, retention, diagnostics and startup behavior.
judgement.why: The rules require cleanup first and retry later but do not determine whether the current start or run continues after cleanup failure.

topics.topic: Failure precedence when multiple checks fail within one stage
questions: When several checks in one stage fail, which failure is returned—for example two invalid values, or an archived project together with an ineligible customer or id conflict?
When several checks in the same stage fail, which failure wins—for example two missing referenced records, several invalid values, or an archived project combined with an ineligible customer?
When two checks in the same stage fail, which refusal takes precedence?

quotes:
Every operation — read or change, of a service, Kernel or the owner —
   checks in one order, and the first failure is its answer; a stage that
   does not apply to it is skipped, and each check an operation states belongs
   to the stage of its kind: (1) the caller's authentication and its right to
   the operation (A09) — for the owner, a valid owner session, then its CSRF
   value, then a confirmation value where one is asked (A13);
   (2) for agent authority, the session and its set (A10), whose refusal
   hides every later failure; (3) that the record named exists; (4) the
   values given (A02, A08, A22); (5) the stated revision or access version
   (A12); (6) the record's lifecycle — archived, erased, anonymised, not in the
   set, a customer's eligibility, a conflict.
judgement.divergence: One implementation returns the first failing check in a fixed internal order within the stage; another returns a different same-stage failure. Callers notice different refusal answers for the same request.
judgement.why: A04 orders the stages but does not order multiple checks within stages 3, 4 or 6.

topics.topic: Interoperable authenticated-encryption and envelope format for backups
questions: What exact authenticated-encryption and backup-envelope format must every implementation use, and which metadata is authenticated?
What cryptographic format makes confidentiality and integrity testable and prevents undetected modification of the unencrypted metadata or ciphertext?
What cryptographic construction makes backup confidentiality and tamper detection testable and interoperable across releases?

quotes:
Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its
   making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
judgement.why: This is the same backup authenticated-encryption and envelope-format question already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Mandatory interoperable authenticated-encryption format for backups
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Same-day retry policy and persistence after a failed daily backup attempt
questions: Does a failed attempt count as that day's one run, and may a later restart on the same UTC day retry it?
Does another restart on the same UTC day retry the failed catch-up, or does the one-run-per-day limit postpone retry until the next day, and where is a failed attempt remembered across restarts?
After today's scheduled attempt fails, may a restart or another trigger retry during the same UTC day?

quotes:
A run that 03:00 found Registry stopped is made when
   it next starts with its service tokens, if no backup was made that UTC
   day; an owner-only start makes no run (rule 10); besides the run after
   an accepted import (A16), there is at most one run per UTC day, and runs
   never overlap.

A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file, writes a
   diagnostic that names the failure and no value (A17), and is tried again at
   the next run; Registry keeps serving.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats a failed attempt as the day's run and waits until the next day; another retries on a later same-day restart because no backup was made. The owner notices different recovery-point age and retry timing.
judgement.why: The text does not say whether a failed attempt consumes the one ordinary run allowed for that UTC day or how that fact survives restart.

topics.topic: Fields and equivalence rules that define a matching create or publish replay
questions: What is semantic equality for every create input, especially structured characteristics: exact encoded representation, ordered structure, or canonical value equality?

Is the authenticated principal or Kernel session part of equality for a publish replay, or may another authorized principal using the same request id and supplied pointer values receive the existing pointer?

quotes:
A create whose request id such a record carries is
   a repeat when the facts it supplies equal that record's current facts of
   the same kind: Registry answers the record as it stands now and changes
   nothing.

Facts are compared as A02 reads them: a required value as written, an
   optional value given blank the same as one not given.

The pointer records its publisher: Kernel for the agent naming the session,
   or the owner (M05). A withdrawal records its principal the same way.
judgement.divergence: One implementation compares structured inputs by canonical domain value and excludes the derived publisher; another compares encoded structure or includes the authenticated principal or Kernel session. Authorized callers notice whether a replay returns the existing record or is refused.
judgement.why: A01 defines blank-value comparison but does not define equality for structured facts or whether derived publisher facts participate in publish-replay equality.

topics.topic: Handling and selection of duplicate project IDs in an import
questions: How is a project selected when two project records have the same id, and is that duplicate checked before selection or only after one of those records is considered picked?
If duplicate project ids occur, is the whole upload unusable, are both duplicate records considered picked together, or may the owner leave them unpicked and import other projects?

quotes:
As the owner picks projects,
   the mapping shows for the picks only: their rooms and pointers; the display
   name and alias each will arrive under — its v1 name and no alias unless the
   owner gives others (R0-85), a name being required (A02).

and every malformed record and every id that
   conflicts with one production holds.

Registry checks what the picks bring in — each picked project with the
   rooms and pointers that name it and the v1 value it names — and nothing
   else of the file; a room or pointer naming another project belongs to that
   project: records only of projects the owner did not pick are neither checked,
   shown as conflicts nor imported, and take no part in the duplicate-id
   check.
judgement.why: Rule 1 says the mapping shows every malformed record, while rule 3 says records belonging only to unpicked projects are not checked, creating incompatible treatment of duplicate project ids before an unambiguous pick exists.

topics.topic: Import-file digest algorithm, input representation, and collision handling
questions: Which collision-resistant algorithm is used, and is the digest over the exact uploaded bytes or over a parsed or canonicalised representation?
How is the import-file digest computed, and what happens if two different uploaded byte sequences have the same digest?

quotes: The mapping names the file by its digest.

What Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States
5 and 6.
judgement.why: This is the same import-file digest algorithm and byte-representation question already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Algorithm and byte representation for import-file digests
quotes: The mapping names the file by its digest.
What Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States 5 and 6.
precedent.why: The digest algorithm, canonical byte representation and encoded digest form are format and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: MigrationClosure cardinality across disaster-recovery histories
questions: Is the at-most-one invariant scoped to an installation or instance across disaster recovery, or only to one store history?
Does "at most one per instance" mean one across the instance's entire disaster-recovery lineage or one in each store history?

quotes:
The restored store begins its own history from the
   backup: every change after it is lost, the audit entries with it, and
   Registry's guarantees — the log's numbering, the closed import — hold
   within each store's history.

A store lost before a checked backup holds the import
loses the import with it, and the import may then be made again.

None; absent, then present for the rest of the store's history. A store
restored after a loss from a backup made before the import begins a history
without it (R0-89).
judgement.why: The later disaster-recovery rule expressly scopes the closed import and its closure to each store history, allowing a new closure after restoration from a pre-import backup.

topics.topic: Owner-session cookie attributes, scope, and HTTP transport rules
questions: What exact cookie attributes and transport rule carry an owner session, including whether a locally reached interface may use the cookie over HTTP?
What exact cookie attributes and deployment constraint make "only to Registry's own origin" true, especially when local access may use HTTP or another service shares the host?

quotes:
The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner
   session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over
   HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only
   to Registry's own origin.
judgement.why: This is the same owner-session cookie attributes, scope and transport-policy question already assigned to State 6.

quotes: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
precedent.why: Exact cookie attributes, host/path scope and SameSite transport policy are HTTP contract and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Permitted relationships between store and backup locations
questions: What path relationships and filesystem object types are valid for the store and backup location, and which unsafe configurations must stop startup?
Which overlap or aliasing relationships between the store and backup locations are accepted or refused?

quotes:
The configuration holds exactly these items and no other: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four: Registry then serves the owner interface alone
   and refuses every service call (A18 rule 10).

The backup location must exist and let Registry create
   and remove a file in it; otherwise the start fails. When the store's
   configured file does not exist and its directory does, Registry makes a new,
   empty store of the running release's version there at the start; otherwise
   the store must open for reading and writing and carry the store
   version of the running release, and a store of another version, or one
   that does not open, fails the start — bringing a store to a new version is
   a step of the release, not of the start.
judgement.divergence: One implementation accepts equal, nested or symlink-aliased store and backup locations; another refuses some or all such relationships at startup. The owner notices different startup acceptance and potentially different backup or retention effects.
judgement.why: A17 validates each location separately but leaves their permitted relationship and aliasing behavior open.

topics.topic: Persistence of successful create replays after related data or types are removed
questions: Does removal of an artifact type invalidate a replay of a publish that already succeeded, or does the request id still return the existing pointer?
Must a request id remain reserved after project anonymisation/deletion or Customer erasure, or may a late replay create a second record?

quotes:
A repeat passes stages (1) to (4) of A04 rule 6 like any call — rights,
   the session's set, the existence of its project, its values, a publish's
   type among them (A22) — and, for 'add a room' and 'publish an artifact
   pointer', the check that its project is not archived (R0-17, R0-88).

Repeating a publish after its type was removed is refused as an unknown
    type (A22).

A request id leaves its record with the values anonymisation or erasure
   removes (M01, M04); a create arriving after that with the same request id
   is a new create.
judgement.why: A01 explicitly rechecks a publish's current type and refuses a replay after removal, while also explicitly allowing a former request id to create anew after anonymisation or erasure removes it.

topics.topic: Representation and byte sequence used for configuration-secret validation
questions: Which bytes are counted and compared: literal configuration bytes, UTF-8 encoding, decoded base64 or hexadecimal bytes, or another fixed representation?
What representation is accepted, and over which byte sequence are length, equality and constant-time comparison defined?

quotes:
A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at
   least 32 bytes long; a shorter one fails the start.

A presented secret is compared in constant time; no secret enters a record,
   a log line, an audit entry, a diagnostic or an answer (R0-23, R0-37).
judgement.why: The accepted textual or binary representation, decoding and exact byte sequence are encoding and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Stage at which related-record existence is checked
questions: At which stage is existence of a newly named customer checked, and does an unknown customer win before value and revision failures or only with the other customer-eligibility checks at stage 6?
Does existence at stage (3) cover every referenced record, such as the customer and project named by one action, or only the action's primary target, leaving related-record existence to stage (6)?

quotes:
Every operation — read or change, of a service, Kernel or the owner —
   checks in one order, and the first failure is its answer; a stage that
   does not apply to it is skipped, and each check an operation states belongs
   to the stage of its kind: (1) the caller's authentication and its right to
   the operation (A09) — for the owner, a valid owner session, then its CSRF
   value, then a confirmation value where one is asked (A13);
   (2) for agent authority, the session and its set (A10), whose refusal
   hides every later failure; (3) that the record named exists; (4) the
   values given (A02, A08, A22); (5) the stated revision or access version
   (A12); (6) the record's lifecycle — archived, erased, anonymised, not in the
   set, a customer's eligibility, a conflict.

A correction newly naming a customer is checked as State 0 says: unknown,
   erased, restricted or ended refused (R0-16, R0-51, R0-57). Keeping the
   customer already named is not newly naming it.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats every referenced record's existence as stage 3, so an unknown customer precedes invalid values and stale revisions; another treats only the primary target at stage 3 and checks the customer with eligibility at stage 6. The owner notices different refusal precedence.
judgement.why: A04 does not define whether 'the record named' includes related records newly referenced by the action.

topics.topic: Create-replay behavior for commits lost by backup restoration

topics.topic: Field constraints applied to malformed imported records
questions: Which State 1 and State 6 field constraints, beyond the cases enumerated in A16 rule 4, are applied to brought-in records?

topics.topic: Handling collisions involving newly minted customer identities

topics.topic: Imported records allowed to reference rooms and the required relationship

topics.topic: Last-audit-sequence value for an empty store
questions: What value is recorded and checked when the backup contains no audit entries?

topics.topic: Owner sessions terminated by one sign-out
questions: Which owner sessions does one sign-out terminate?

topics.topic: Pending-confirmation state after submitting a different value to an expired confirmation
questions: If the pending confirmation has expired and the submission supplies a different value, is the expired pending confirmation cleared or retained?

topics.topic: Permitted filesystem side effects and validation order during failed startup
questions: May a failed start leave behind a newly created store or probe file, and in what order are non-mutating validation, path probing, and store creation performed?

topics.topic: Registry ownership and permitted handling of files in the backup location
questions: Which files in the configured backup location may Registry inspect or delete?

topics.topic: Scope of import mapping validation and reporting
questions: Does the mapping report and validate malformed records and conflicting ids throughout the file, or only within the selected projects and the records they bring?

topics.topic: Service-token configuration requirements in owner-only mode
questions: Does the required test apply only to a partially populated service-token set, or should absence of Client Portal's token also reject owner-only mode?

topics.topic: Session state retained after refused import confirmation
questions: After a refused import confirmation, which session state remains: the uploaded file, mapping inputs or picks, and any pending confirmation?

topics.topic: Stage and timing of confirmation-binding checks
questions: Are the confirmation's action, target, revision or access version, and input bindings all checked in stage (1), or are they checked in their ordinary value, revision, and lifecycle stages after the value has been consumed?

topics.topic: Store-level checks required to verify a backup
questions: What exact store-level verification constitutes a passed checked backup, beyond opening it, matching its version and checking the audit sequence?

topics.topic: UTC date used to validate an audit-erasure request
questions: If an erasure request crosses UTC midnight, is its date validated against the date when the request arrives, when the value check runs, or when the transaction commits?

topics.topic: Whether a one-time import may be completed with no selected projects
questions: May the owner successfully close the one-time import while selecting zero projects?

topics.topic: Whether an import backup satisfies the ordinary daily backup requirement
questions: If a checked import backup succeeds before 03:00 UTC, or before a catch-up start later that day, must the ordinary daily run still occur?

topics.topic: Whether backup creation or verification failure postpones retention deletion
questions: Does failure of creating or checking the new backup delay deletion of backups older than 30 days, or does only a deletion failure delay it?
